newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ACCC sees major changes in Australian bank market.
newsitem.headline: ACCC sees major changes in Australian bank market.

text.p: Australia's anti-monopolies authority, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), said on Friday there had been significant changes in the banking industry since it last made a decision on regional bank mergers in September 1995.

"In particular, increased competition from mortgage originators have not only forced banks to cut rates sharply, but also has led to more product unbundling," ACCC chairman Alan Fels said in a statement.
Fels said this had influenced the ACCC's analysis of the state of competition in the Victorian market as part of its ruling on Westpac Banking Corp's A$1.44 billion bid for Bank of Melbourne.
The ACCC, Treasurer Peter Costello and the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) all announced earlier on Friday they had approved the merger between the two banks, first announced in April.
"Like the Wallis committee, however, the ACCC still sees signficant elements of the banking market as being regional in character," Fels said.

Fels said the commission's evaluation of the Westpac-Bank of Melbourne merger was based on the conclusion that although some product clustering still occurred, there were a large number of consumers who would shop around from difference suppliers to get the best deal.

"BML has traditionally been strong in the home loan sector However, the national market for home loans is not highly concentrated and competition from non-bank financial institutions have forced interst rates down to a competitive level," fels said.
He said this was likely to continue after the merger and so there would be no competition problem in this market.
